x: God Almighty says: All thanks and all praise are due to the One Who is worshipped, Who is the Owner of everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths, apart from everything that they worship and apart from everything else. There is no Owner of any of that other than Him. So the meaning is: He Who is the Owner of all of it, And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. He says: All thanks are due to Him in the Hereafter, just as that is due to Him in this immediate world, because from Him are all blessings upon everyone in the heavens and the earth in this world, and from Him will be that in the Hereafter. So all praise is due to God alone, apart from anything else in this immediate world and the hereafter, because all blessings are from Him, and no one shares them with Him besides Him. He is the Wise in His management of His creation and His dispensing of them according to His decree. He is aware of them and what is good for them, and of what they have done and what they will do. He encompasses all of that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And He is the Wise, the All-Aware. Wise in His affair, All-Aware of His creation.

x: God Almighty says: He knows what enters the earth and what disappears from it, from their saying: I entered such-and-such: if I entered it, as the poet said: I saw the rhymes swaying in a melodious manner, and it was difficult for needles to insert them. What he means by his saying: They enter into entrances: They enter entrances. And what comes out of it means: And what comes out of the earth. And what descends from the sky and what ascends therein means: And what ascends in the sky. This is report from God that He is the All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden in the heavens and the earth, of what is apparent in them and what is hidden. He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving. He is the Most Merciful to the people of repentance among His servants, that He does not punish them after their repentance. He is the Forgiver of their sins if they repent from them.

God the Most High says: And those of your people who denied God's ability to recreate Him after their annihilation in the form they were in before their annihilation urge you, O Muhammad, to hasten the coming of the Hour, mocking your promise to them and denying your report. Say to them: Yes, by my Lord, it will come to you. I swear by Him that the Hour will come to you. Then He, the Most High, returned after mentioning the Hour to Himself and glorifying it, and said, Knower of the unseen. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it ‘Alim al-Ghaib’ in the nominative case as a resumption, since there was a barrier between His statement and my Lord and His statement the Knower of the Unseen.

Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as ‘Alim’ in the fa’il form, but they lowered ‘Alim’ in response to His statement and my Lord as it was a description of Him. The rest of the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as ‘Alam al-Ghaib in the fa’il form, and in the genitive case, they responded to its i’rab as it was a description of Him. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that all of these three readings are well-known readings among the reciters of the regions and have similar meanings, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct. However, the most amazing reading in this regard is that I read with it ‘Alam al-Ghaib in accordance with the reading that I mentioned from the majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa. As for choosing ‘Alam over ‘Aalam, it is because it is more expressive in praising. As for the genitive case in it, it is because it is an attribute of the Lord, and it is in the accusative case.
What He meant by His saying
h
Knower of the Unseen is the Knower of what is hidden from the sight of creation

, so that no one sees it, either what He did not create from what He will create, or what He created and no one but Him was informed of it. Rather, He, may His praise be glorified, described Himself in this place with His knowledge of the unseen, informing His creation that no one knows the time of the Hour except Him, even if it is coming. So He said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to those who disbelieve in their Lord: Yes, by your Lord, the Hour will surely come to you. But no one knows the time of its coming except the Knower of the Unseen, from whom not an atom’s weight is hidden. What He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
It is not hidden from Him
, is that it is not absent from Him, but it is apparent to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
It is not hidden from Him
, he said: It is not absent from Him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Nothing is hidden from Him, he said: It is not absent.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Not even an atom’s weight escapes Him: meaning, it does not disappear from Him. We have already explained this with supporting evidence in what has preceded, so there is no need to repeat it here. And His statement, the weight of an atom means: the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth. God Almighty says: Nothing, the weight of an atom or greater or lesser, is hidden from Him, wherever it is in the heavens or on the earth. Nor less than that means: Nothing smaller than the weight of an atom or greater than that is hidden from Him, except in a clear book means: It is established in a book that makes clear to the one looking at it that God Almighty has established it, counted it, and known it, so nothing is hidden from His knowledge.

However, the most amazing reading in this regard is that I read with it ‘Alam al-Ghaib in accordance with the reading that I mentioned from the majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa.

x: God Almighty says: He established this in the clear Book, so that those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God and His Messenger commanded them to do, and refrained from what He forbade them from, may be established in their obedience to their Lord. For them is forgiveness God Almighty says: For those who believed and did righteous deeds, there is forgiveness from their Lord for their sins. And a generous provision He says: And a pleasant life on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: For them is forgiveness for their sins and generous provision in Paradise.

x: God Almighty says: He established this in the Book, so that He may reward the believers with what He has described, and so that He may reward those who strive to defeat Our verses. He says: And so that He may establish those who worked to invalidate Our proofs and arguments, helping them, who think that they can outsmart Us by themselves, so that We cannot overpower them. For them is a punishment. He says: For them is a punishment of the most severe and painful punishment, and by painful He means: painful. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, They strive against Our signs, trying to outsmart them: meaning, they will not be able to outsmart them. For them is a punishment of a painful torment. He said: The torment is the worst of the torment, and the painful is the hurtful.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And those who strive to frustrate Our verses, he said: Strive to nullify or invalidate them, he said: And they are the polytheists, and he recited, Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it that you may overcome
r
(Fussilat 41:26)

x: God Almighty says: He established this in a clear Book, that He may reward those who believe and those who strive in Our verses with what has been made clear to them, and that those who have been given knowledge may see. See is in the accusative case in apposition to His statement: rewards, in His statement, that He may reward those who have believed. What is meant by those who have been given knowledge are the Muslims among the People of the Book, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his peers who had read the books of God that were revealed before the Criterion. So God Almighty said: And that these who have been given knowledge may see by the Book of God, which is the Torah, the Book that has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord, that it is the truth. It was said: What is meant by those who were given knowledge are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth. He said: The companions of Muhammad. His statement,
h
And guides to the path of the Almighty

, the Praiseworthy, means: And He guides those who follow it and act in accordance with it to the path of God, the Almighty, in His vengeance against His enemies, the Praiseworthy before His creation, so His favors are with them and His blessings are with them. What he means is that the Book that was revealed to Muhammad guides to Islam.

x: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, astonished at His promise to them of resurrection to one another after death, Shall we direct you, O people, to a man who will inform you that when you are torn apart, you will indeed be in a new creation? That is, he will inform you that after you have been scattered across the earth by a calamity and after your fate in the dust as remains, you will return to your state before death, a new creation.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And those who disbelieved said, ‘Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, when you are dispersed to every fragment?’ That was said by the polytheists of Quraysh and the polytheists among the people, who will inform you, when you are dispersed to every fragment?: when the earth consumes you, and you become dust and bones, and wild beasts and birds tear you apart, that you will indeed be in a new creation. You will be brought to life and resurrected.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in His statement, Shall We direct you to a man... to a new creation, he said: He says, When you are torn apart, and when you have decayed and become bones, dust, and dust, that is, Every one torn apart, indeed you will be in a new creation. He said: He informs you that you, so the kasra of if did not work in informs you in it, but he began with it as an initiation, because the report is report and a statement, so the kasra in if is for the meaning of the narration in His statement, informs you, not its wording, as if it was said: It was said to you, Indeed you will be in a new creation.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by those who disbelieved in Him and denied that He would send some of them to others after death, amazed by the promise He made to them by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you think this one who promises us that after we are all torn apart in a new creation is a lie to God, so you create falsehood against Him and fabricate falsehood against Him? Or is he mad? He says: Or is he crazy and speaks what has no meaning. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: They said, in denial: Does he invent a lie against God? He said: They said: Either he is lying about God, or he is mad, or he is insane. Rather, those who do not believe... the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Then some of them said to one another, Does he invent a lie against God, or is he mad? The man is crazy and speaks what he does not understand. So God said, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment and in extreme error. And His statement, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment and far astray, says the Most High: The matter is not as these polytheists said about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they thought that he had fabricated a lie against God, or that he was in heaven. Rather, those among these polytheists who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in God’s torment in the Hereafter, and will stray far from the path of truth and the straight path. For this reason, they say what they say about him.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said:
m: God said, Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in punishment and far error, and He ordered him to swear to them so that they would take heed. He recited, Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did.' At-Taghabun 64:7... the entire verse. He recited, Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.' Saba' 34:3. The alif in the phrase Has he invented something about God was cut off in the cutting and connecting, so it was opened because it is an alif of interrogation. As for the alif that comes after it, which is an alif of ifta'ala, it was dropped because it is a light, extra letter that is dropped in connected speech. Similar to it are: It is the same for them whether I seek forgiveness for them Al-Munafiqun 60:6, I was arrogant with my own hand Sad 75, I chose the daughters Saffat 37:153, and the like. As for the alif of now and those who remember, this one was lengthened, and that one was not, because alan and al-dhakireen were open, so if it had been dropped, there would have been no difference between the question and the report, so the lengthening in them was made a difference between the question and the report, and the alif of the question is open, so they were separated by that, so that is more indicative of the difference than the lengthening.

x: God Almighty says: Have these deniers of the Resurrection, those who reject the Resurrection after death, who say to Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Does he invent a lie against God, or is there madness in him? not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heavens and the earth, and knew that wherever they were, My earth and heavens surround them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, so that they would be deterred from their ignorance and refrain from denying Our signs, lest We command the earth to swallow them up, or the heaven to fall upon them completely? For if We will, We will do that to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them

? He said: They look to their right and to their left, how the sky has encompassed them. If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up, just as We caused those who were before them to swallow up. Or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them, meaning pieces of the sky. And His statement,
h
Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns [to God]

, the Most High says: Indeed in the heaven and earth encompassing the servants of God is a sign: that is, a sign for every servant who turns [to God]: that is, for every servant who turns to his Lord in repentance, and returns to knowing His Oneness, and acknowledging His Lordship, and recognizing His Oneness, and submitting to His obedience, on the condition that the one who does that is not prevented from doing anything he wants to do, nor is it difficult for him to do anything he wants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back. The one who turns back is the one who repents.

x: God Almighty says: And We had certainly given David bounty from Us, and We said to the mountains, ‘Repeat with him.’ Glorify God with him when he glorifies God. Returning among the Arabs means returning, and a man spending the night in his home and with his family.
Two days, one day of gatherings and clubs, one day of marching to the enemies for retribution Any return.

Some of them read it as Obei ma'ah from Ab ya'ub, meaning: deal with him, and that is a reading that I do not permit reading because it is contrary to the reading of the argument. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told me: Abu Kudayna told us, and Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Recite with him means: Pray with him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, O mountains, echo with him, meaning: Glorify with him.

c: Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Ala’i told us: Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman:
m: O mountains, echo with him, meaning: glorify God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah:
m: O mountains, echo with him. He said: Praise God in the language of Abyssinia.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify with him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: O mountains, echo with him: meaning, glorify with him when he glorifies.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, O mountains, echo with him, he said: Glorify with him. He said: And the birds as well.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, O mountains, echo with Him, that he said: Glorify Him.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement, O mountains, echo with him, glorify him. And his saying, and the birds. There are two views regarding the accusative case of the bird: One of them is what Ibn Zayd said, that the bird was called as the mountains were called, so it is accusative because it is conjoined to a nominative case, in a way that does not make it appropriate to repeat its nominative case, so it is like a verbal noun in its own right. The other is: a verb with an omitted pronoun that is not indicated by the speech, so the meaning of the speech is: So We said: O mountains, echo with him, and We subjected the birds to him. If it is raised in response to what is in his saying:
h
Glorify the mountains

, it is permissible. It is also permissible to raise the bird while it is conjoined to the mountains, even if it is not appropriate to call it with the way the mountains were called, so it is as the poet said. Except, O Amr and Ad-Dahhak, walk, for you have crossed the road’s vineyard. His saying,
h
And We made iron soft for him
, mentioned that the iron was in his hand like wet clay, and he could use it in his hand as he wished, without using fire or striking it with iron.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We made iron soft for him
means God made iron subservient to him without fire.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Uthma told us: Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We made the iron soft for him
, he would straighten it with his hand, and not put it in fire, nor strike it with iron.

evidence.text: Some of them read it as Obei ma'ah from Ab ya'ub, meaning: deal with him, and that is a reading that I do not permit reading because it is contrary to the reading of the argument.

Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told me: Abu Kudayna told us, and Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Recite with him means: Pray with him.

x: And his saying, Make sabaghat, means: We ordered him to make sabaghat, which are complete twin coats of mail. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Make coats of mail, meaning armor. The first to make them was David. Before that, they were only plates.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
Make long coats of mail
, he said: The long coats of mail are iron armor. His saying,
h
And measured in the chain
, the people of interpretation differed regarding the chain.

x: Some of them said: The chain is the nail of the collar of the armor.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And he measured the chains. He said: He would make them without fire, nor strike them with iron, then he would chain them together. Chains are the nails in the throat.

x: Others said: It is the throat itself.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And measured in the chain
, he said: The chain is its ring, meaning the amount of those rings. He said: And the poet said: Al-Masdi narrated it well and humiliated it He said: He said: He expanded it and shaved it well.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: And measure in the chain. By chain, he means: the hole in the armor, so that its collar is plugged.

x: Some of the people of knowledge of Arabic speech said: It is said that a chained armor is: if its collar is nailed, and he cited as evidence for this saying the saying of the poet: And upon them are two chains of narration, which David ruled or the making of the heavy-duty swords followed. It was said: God said to David, And measure out the chains, because there were previously plates.
Who said that?

c: Nasr ibn Ali told us: My father told us: Khalid ibn Qays told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And measure the number of chains
. He said: They were plates, so he ordered that they be chained together into rings. What he meant by his saying,
h
And measure the number of chains

is: He measured the nails in the rings of the armor so that it would be of such size that the nail would not become too thick, nor the ring too narrow, so that the ring would break, nor the ring too wide, nor the nails too small and small, so that they would fit neatly in the ring. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And measure the length of the chain, he said: The length of the nails and the rings. Do not hammer the nails so that they become smooth, and do not sharpen them, Muhammad ibn Amr said, and Al-Harith said: so that they become broken.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
and measure the chain
, he said: Do not make the nail too small and the ring too large, lest it become untidy, and do not make the nail too large and the ring too small, lest the nail break.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And measure the chain

, he said: Do not make the nail too thick, lest it break the ring, and do not make it too thin, lest it become loose. And His statement, And do righteous deeds, means that God Almighty says: And, O David, you and your family, work in obedience to God. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do, meaning that God Almighty says: I am Seeing of what you and your followers do, and nothing of it is hidden from Me, and I will reward you and them for all of that.

x: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, And to Solomon was the wind. The majority of reciters in the regions read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, with the wind in the accusative case, meaning: And We gave David a favor from Us, and We subjected the wind to Solomon. Asim read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, in the nominative case with the adjective, since the accusative case was not apparent. The correct reading of this in our view is the accusative, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And His saying,
h
Its morning is a month

, God Almighty says: And We subjected to Solomon the wind, its morning journey until midday is a month’s journey, and its evening journey from midday until night is a month’s journey. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “
h
And to Solomon We subjected the wind

: its morning journey was a month’s journey and its evening journey was a month’s journey.” He said: It goes in the morning a month’s journey, and it comes in the evening a month’s journey. He said: It goes in the morning a month’s journey and it comes in the evening a month’s journey.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: h
And to Solomon We subjected the wind

, its morning journey was a month and its evening journey was a month. He said: It was mentioned to me that there was a house on the bank of the Tigris in which was written a letter written by some of Solomon’s companions, either from the jinn or from mankind: We have settled it and we did not build it, and we found it built. We went out from Istakhr and said it, and we are returning from it, God willing, so we will spend the night in Syria.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And to Solomon We subjected the wind

, its morning journey being a month and its evening journey being a month, he said: He had a wooden ship, and on it were a thousand corners, in each corner a thousand chambers in which the jinn and humans rode, under each corner a thousand devils, they and the winds would raise that ship, and when it was lifted the wind would come gently and move with it, and they would move with it. He would take a nap with a people who were a month apart from him, and he would spend the evening with a people who were a month apart from him, and the people would not know until the armies and soldiers had shaded them with him.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, And to Solomon was the wind.

The majority of reciters in the regions read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, with the wind in the accusative case, meaning: And We gave David a favor from Us, and We subjected the wind to Solomon.
Asim read it as, And to Solomon was the wind, in the nominative case with the adjective, since the accusative case was not apparent.
The correct reading of this in our view is the accusative, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

m: Al-Mansa’ah is the stick. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying Mansatuhu. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the people of Basra recited it as Mansatuhu without a hamza. The one who found fault with the reciter of that from the people of Basra claimed that the mansat is the stick, and that its origin is from Nasa’at bihi al-Ghanam. He would say to it, ‘What is your name?’ It would say, ‘So-and-so.’ He would say, ‘You are nothing.’ If it was planted, it would be planted, and if it was used for medicine, it would be written down. While he was praying one day, he saw a tree in front of him. He said to it, ‘What is your name?’ It said, ‘The carob tree.’ He said, ‘What are you for?’ It said, ‘For the destruction of this House.’ So Solomon said, ‘O God, conceal my death from the jinn so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen.’ So he carved it into a staff and leaned on it for a year while the jinn were working.

But the termites ate it, and he fell down. It became clear to mankind that if the jinn knew the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating torment for a year.” He said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to recite it like this. He said: So the jinn thanked the termites. She used to bring her water.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,

He entered it on the occasion that he died, and that was because there was not a day in which he woke up without a tree growing on it, and he would ask it, ‘What is your name?’ The tree would say, ‘My name is such and such.’ He would say to it, ‘Why did it grow?’ It would say, ‘It grew for such and such.’ He would order it to be cut down. If it grew for planting, he would plant it, and if it grew for medicine, it would say, ‘It grew for medicine for such and such.’ He would make it like that, until a tree grew called Al-Kharuba. He asked it, ‘What is your name?’ It said to him, ‘I am Al-Kharuba.’ He would say, ‘Why did it grow?’ It said, ‘To destroy this mosque.’ Solomon said, ‘What was God like?’” To destroy it while I am alive, you are the one upon whose face is my destruction and the destruction of the Holy House. So he took it off and planted it in his wall, then he entered the sanctuary, and stood praying leaning on his staff, and he died without the devils knowing about it, and they worked for him, fearing that he would come out and punish them. The devils used to gather around the sanctuary, and the sanctuary had windows in front of it and behind it, and the devil who wanted to take it off would say: Are you not a skin if you enter? So I came out from the other side, and one of those devils entered and passed by, and no devil looked at Solomon in the sanctuary except that he burned, so he passed by and did not hear the voice of Solomon, peace be upon him, then he returned and did not hear, then he returned and fell in the house and did not burn, and he saw that Solomon had fallen, so he went out and told the people that Solomon had died, so they opened it and took him out and found his staff, which is the staff in the Ethiopian language, that the termites had eaten it, and they did not know how long he had died, so they put the termites on the staff, and it ate from it for a day and a night, then they calculated in that manner and found that he had died a year ago. And in the reading of Ibn Masʿud: So they continued to strive for him after his death for a full year. Then the people became certain that the jinn had been lying to them, and if they had known the unseen, they would have known of Solomon’s death, and they would not have remained in the torment for a year working for him. This is the saying of God: “Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth that gnawed at his staff.
h
So when he fell down

, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.” He says: Their matter became clear to the people that they had been lying to them. Then the devils said to the termite: If you were eating food, we would have brought you the best food, and if you were drinking drink, we would have given you the best drink, but we will transfer water and clay to you. So what is inside the wood is what the devils bring to it as thanks for it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The jinn used to tell mankind that they knew things of the unseen, and that they knew what would happen tomorrow. So they were tested by the death of Solomon, so he died and remained on his staff for a year, and they were not aware of his death, and they were subjected to that year, working diligently. So when he came out, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. And they had remained diligently and working for him for a year.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,

Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff

, he said: Solomon said to the Angel of Death: O Angel of Death, when you command me, inform me. He said: So he came to him and said: O Solomon, I have commanded you, you have only a short time left. He said: Then the Angel of Death entered upon him and took his soul while he was leaning on his staff, and he did not do that to escape from the Angel of Death. He said: And the jinn were working in front of him and looking at him, thinking that he was alive. He said: Then God sent a creature of the earth. He said: When the jinn saw that, they dispersed and left. That is what His statement,

Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff

. He said: The stick is the mansa’ah. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Solomon, son of David, was praying. He Surat Saba 34:14 So when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth that gnawed at his staff.

, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. died while he was praying, and the jinn were working, unaware of his death, until the termites ate away at his staff, and he fell down. c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Kalbi, on the authority of Yahya ibn Haniʿ, on the authority of Urwah al-Muradi, on the authority of a man among them called Furwah ibn Masik, who said:
m: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, tell me about Saba’. Was it a man, a woman, a mountain, or animals?’ He said, ‘No, he was an Arab man who had ten sons. Six of them were considered auspicious and four were considered unlucky. As for those who were considered auspicious from him, they were Kindah, Himyar, Azd, the Ashʿariyyun, Madhhij, and Anmar, from whom came Khatham and Bajila. As for those who were considered unlucky, they were ʿAmilah, Judham, Lakhm, and Ghassan.”
b.via: a man among them called Furwah ibn Masik

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan bin Al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Abu Sabrah Al-Nakha’i narrated to us, on the authority of Furwah bin Masik Al-Qat’i, who said:
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’, what is it? A land or a woman? He said: It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man who gave birth to ten children, six of whom were on the right and four on the left. As for those who were on the wrong, they were Lakhm, Judham, Amla, and Ghassan. As for those who were on the right, they were Kinda, Al-Ash’ariyyun, Al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar, and Anmar. A man said: Who are Anmar? He said: Those from whom are Khatham and Bajila.” Abu Kurayb narrated: Al-Anqazi narrated:

c: Asbat bin Nasr informed me, on the authority of Yahya bin Hani’ Al-Muradi, on the authority of his father,
m: or on the authority of his uncle Asbat is uncertain, who said: “Farwa bin Masik came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’, was it a mountain or a land?’ He said: ‘It was neither a mountain nor a land, but rather a man from the Arabs who gave birth to ten tribes.’ Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: ‘And Anmar, who say that they are from Bajila and Khatham.’ So if the matter is as narrated from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that Saba’ was a man, then the pronunciation and non-pronunciation are moderate. As for the pronunciation, it is the name of a well-known man, and as for leaving the pronunciation, it is the name of a tribe or a land. And scholars among the reciters have recited each of them.” The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase in their dwellings. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it in their dwellings in the plural, meaning the dwellings of the family of Saba. The majority of the Kufic reciters read it in their dwelling in the singular and with a kasra on the kaf, which is the language of the people of Yemen as far as I was told. Hamza read it their dwelling in the singular and with a fatha on the kaf. The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is that all of these readings have similar meanings, so whichever one recites them, he is correct. We have already explained the meaning of his statement, a sign. As for his statement,

two gardens on the right and on the left
, he means two gardens between two mountains, on the right and left of whoever approaches them. Their description, as mentioned to us, was as follows:
