, he said: There were two gardens between two mountains, and a woman would take out her bucket on her head and walk between two mountains, and her bucket would fill up without her hand touching it. But when they transgressed, God sent against them a creature called Jarth, which dug into them and drowned them, and nothing remained for them except tamarisk and a few lote trees.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement, There was certainly for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign -
h
two gardens on the right and on the left

... to the statement, But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, he said: Not a single mosquito, fly, flea, scorpion, or snake was seen in their city. Even though caravans would come with lice and insects on their clothes, they would have no sooner looked at their homes than the insects would die. He said: Even though a person would enter two gardens, he would hold a basket over his head, and when he came out, that basket would be full of all kinds of fruit, but he had not taken anything from it with his hand. He said: And the dam watered it. The two gardens were raised in His statement,
h
Two gardens on the right and on the left

, as a translation of the sign, because the meaning of the statement is: There was certainly for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign - two gardens on their right and on their left. And His statement,
h
Eat of the provision of your Lord

, which He provides for you from these two gardens, from their crops and fruits, and be grateful to Him, for what He has bestowed upon you from His provision. And this is the end of the report. Then the report about the town began, and it was said: This is a good town, meaning it is not a salt marsh, but as we mentioned about its description from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, that it was as Ibn Zayd described it, that there was nothing harmful in it, wild animals, creeping things, or insects. And a Forgiving Lord, he says: And a Forgiving Lord of your sins if you obey Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
A good land and a Forgiving Lord
, and your Lord is Forgiving of your sins, a people to whom God has given a blessing, and commanded them to obey Him, and forbade them from disobeying Him.

evidence.text: And scholars among the reciters have recited each of them.”
The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase in their dwellings.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it in their dwellings in the plural, meaning the dwellings of the family of Saba.
The majority of the Kufic reciters read it in their dwelling in the singular and with a kasra on the kaf, which is the language of the people of Yemen as far as I was told.
Hamza read it their dwelling in the singular and with a fatha on the kaf.
The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is that all of these readings have similar meanings, so whichever one recites them, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says: So Sheba turned away from obeying her Lord and turned away from following what her messengers had called her to, that He is her Creator.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, he said:
m: God sent thirteen prophets except for Saba, but they denied them.
h
So We sent upon them the flood of the dam

. God Almighty says: So We pierced their shores when they turned away from believing in Our messengers, with a flood that used to hold back the floods from them. The dam is the well that holds back water. Its singular is dam, and it is what Al-A’sha meant when he said: In that there is a model for the follower and a destination that has been forgotten by the dam. Rajam bint Hamir has donkeys. When their water comes, he does not throw up. The Aram was mentioned as one of the things that Bilqis built.

x: Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi narrated to us, saying: Wahb bin Jarir narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying:
m: I heard Al-Mughirah bin Hakim say: When Bilqis became king, her people started fighting over the water of their valley. She kept forbidding them, but they would not obey her, so she gave up her kingdom and went to her palace and left them. When evil increased between them and they regretted it, they came to her and wanted her to return to her kingdom, but she refused. They said: You must return or we will kill you. She said: You do not obey me, and you do not have minds, and you will not obey me. They said: We will obey you, and we have not found any good in us after you. So she came and ordered that their valley be blocked by a wall. Ahmad said, Wahb said, my father said: I asked Al-Mughirah bin Hakim about Al-Aram, and he said: It is in the words of Himyar Al-Masnat. It blocked the space between the two mountains, so it held back the water from behind the dam, and made for it gates, one above the other, and built a huge pool behind it, and made in it twelve outlets for their rivers. When the rain came, the torrent was held back from behind the dam, so I ordered the upper gate to be opened, and its water flowed into the pool, and I ordered the dung to be thrown into it, and some of the dung came out faster than others. So those rivers continued to narrow, and the dung was sent into the water, until it all came out together, and it was divided between them according to that, until what happened to her and Solomon happened.

c: Ahmad bin Omar Al-Basri told us: Abu Saleh bin Zuraiq told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So We sent upon them the flood of the dam
, he said: Al-Masnat in the Yemeni dialect.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God,
h
The flood of the dam
, he said: severe. And it was said that the dam is the name of a valley belonging to these people.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then We sent upon them the flood of the dam
, he said: It was a valley in Yemen, which flowed to Mecca, and they were given water and their flood would end there.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
So We sent upon them the flood of the dam
. It was mentioned to us that
h
the flood of the dam

was a valley into which streams from various valleys gathered, so they deliberately blocked up the space between the two mountains with pitch and stones, and made gates over it. They would take from its water what they needed, and block off from them whatever part of its water they did not need.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
Then We sent upon them the flood of Al-Arim

, that it was a valley called Al-Arim, and whenever it rained, the valleys of Yemen would flow into Al-Arim, and the water would gather around it. So the Sabaeans went to Al-Arim and blocked the space between the two mountains, and they blocked it with rocks and tar, and it was blocked for a period of time, with no hope of water. He said: They were not afraid.

x: Others said: Al-Aram is an attribute of the land they had, not its name. Surat Saba 34:16 But they turned away,
h
so We sent upon them the flood of the dam
and replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit and tamarisk and a few lote trees.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The flood of the dam

, meaning: the severe one. The reason that caused God to send that flood upon them, as he mentioned to me, was a rat that God sent against their dam, and it made a hole in it. Then the scholars differed about the description of what happened in that hole, which led to the destruction of their two gardens.

x: Some of them said: The description of that was that when the flood found work in the dam, it worked in it, then the water overflowed onto their gardens, drowning them and destroying their land and their homes.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said:
m: They, meaning the Sabaeans, had a dam that they had built as an everlasting structure, and it was what would prevent a flood from reaching their property. It was claimed in their knowledge of their divination that only a mouse could destroy their dam, so they did not leave a crack between two rocks without tying a cat to it. When the time came, and God intended for them to drown, as they say, a red mouse approached one of those cats and harassed it until it was behind it, meaning the cat. It entered the gap that was near it and penetrated the dam, digging in it until it weakened for the flood, and they did not know. When the flood came, it found a hole, so it entered it until it pulled out the dam and flooded the money, carrying it away until nothing remained of it except what God mentioned. When they dispersed, they went to the divination of Imran bin Amir.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When the people abandoned God’s command, God sent upon them a rat called Al-Khald, which pierced their bottom until it flooded their gardens and destroyed their land as punishment for their deeds.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: When they transgressed and rebelled, meaning Saba, God sent a rat against them, which breached the dam on them, and God drowned them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: God sent a rat against them, and gave it power over those who had been holding back the water that was used to irrigate them, so it destroyed the mouths of those stones, and everything in them of lead and other things, until it left them as stones. Then God sent
h
the flood of the dam
, and it uprooted that dam and what it had been holding back, and it uprooted those two gardens, and took them away. He recited:
h
So We sent upon them the flood of the dam
and replaced their two gardens with two gardens. He said: It took away those villages and the two gardens.

x: Others said: The reason for that was that the water they used to fill their gardens flowed to a place other than the place they used to benefit from, and as a result their gardens were ruined.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God sent upon them - meaning upon the dam - a beast from the earth, and it made a hole in it, and that water flowed to a place other than the place from which they had benefited, and God replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter food, and that was when they disobeyed and were arrogant in their living. The first statement is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, as God Almighty mentioned that He sent
h
the flood of the dam
upon them, and that sending it upon them would not have happened except by pouring it upon them, or upon their gardens and their land, not by diverting it from them. And His statement,
h
And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit

, God Almighty says: And We replaced their orchards of fruits with gardens of the harvest of the arak fruit, and the arak is the bitter fruit. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God replaced their two gardens with bitter fruit, and bitter fruit is the arak tree.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan say, regarding His statement, My beings eat bitter fruit, he said: I think he said: bitter fruit is the arak tree.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Abdullah bin Musa told me, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: He ate Khamt. He said: Khamt is the arak tree.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, My own food is bitter, he said: the arak.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: My self eats fermented fruit. And fermented fruit is the arak tree, and its food is the barberry tree.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit
, that God replaced them with gardens of fruits and grapes, as their gardens became bitter, which is the arak tree.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens

, he said: I will take away those towns and gardens and replace for them what I told you with bitter food. He said: The bitter is the arak tree. He said: He replaced the grapes with arak, and the fruit with tamarisk, and some of the few lote trees. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of reciters in the regions read it with the tanween of akal, except for Abu Amr, who adds it to khamat, meaning: those with khamat fruit. As for those who did not add that to khamat, and added the tanween to akal, they considered khamat to be the food, so they returned it to it in its i'rab. The reciters of the regions read it with the damma of the alif and the kaf of akal, except for Nafi', who used to lighten it. The correct reading in my opinion is the reading of those who read it as dhawati akal with a damma on the alif and the kaf due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this, and with the tanween of akal due to the widespread reading in that way among the reciters of the regions, without seeing any error in the reading of those who read it by adding it to the khamt. This is in adding it and not adding it, similar to the Arabs’ saying in the garden of so-and-so: An’ab karem and An’ab karem. Sometimes they add the an’ab to the karem because it is from it, and sometimes they add the tanween, then they translate it as karem because the grapes are the fruit of the vine. As for the tamarisk, it is called tarfa’. It is also said that it is a tree similar to the tamarisk, except that it is larger than it. It is also said that it is the samr.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And tamarisk, he said: tamarisk is the tamarisk tree. And his saying,
h
And some few lote trees
, means: My food is bitter gourd, tamarisk,
h
and some few lote trees
. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: My own food is bitter fruit and tamarisk and a little lote tree. He said: While the tree of the people was the best of trees, God made it one of the worst trees because of their deeds.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this word.
The majority of reciters in the regions read it with the tanween of akal, except for Abu Amr, who adds it to khamat, meaning: those with khamat fruit.
The reciters of the regions read it with the damma of the alif and the kaf of akal, except for Nafi', who used to lighten it.

The correct reading in my opinion is the reading of those who read it as dhawati akal with a damma on the alif and the kaf due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this, and with the tanween of akal due to the widespread reading in that way among the reciters of the regions, without seeing any error in the reading of those who read it by adding it to the khamt.

x: And His statement,
h
That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief

, the Most High says: This that We did to these people of Sheba, by sending upon them the flood of the dam, until their wealth was destroyed and their gardens were ruined, was a recompense from Us for their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our messengers. And that in His statement, That is how We recompensed them is in the accusative case because of the occurrence of We recompensed them for it, and the meaning of the statement is: We recompensed them for that because they disbelieved. And his saying, And shall We reward anyone but the ungrateful? The reciters differed in their recitation of it. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as and shall We reward with a ya and opened the zay as if the subject was not named, except the ungrateful in the nominative case. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as and shall We reward with a noon and with a kasra on the zay “except the ungrateful” in the accusative case.

The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one recites it, the reciter is correct. The meaning of the statement is: Thus did We reward them for their disbelief in God. And who is rewarded except the ungrateful for the blessings of God?
Does God not reward those who believe in Him for their righteous deeds, specifically rewarding those who disbelieve?
Is anyone rewarded except the ungrateful?

It would be said: The recompense in this case is the recompense, and God, the Exalted, promised the people of faith in Him that He would bestow His favor upon them, and that He would reward them for one of their righteous deeds ten times as much, to an endless multiplication. And He promised the sinner among His servants that He would bestow the same amount of bad deeds on them for one of their sins, as a reward for their crime. The reward is for the people of major sins and disbelief, and the recompense is for the people of faith along with His favor. That is why He, the Most High, said in this case: And does He reward except the ungrateful? It is as if He, the Most High, said: No one is rewarded, no one is rewarded for his deeds except the ungrateful, since the reward is like the one for whom he is rewarded, and God does not forgive him any of his sins, nor does He erase any of them in this world.
As for the believer, He bestows His favor upon him as I have described. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And shall We reward? means shall We punish.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief

. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?” When God the Almighty intends to honor a servant, He accepts his good deeds, and when He intends to humiliate a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets him on the Day of Resurrection. He said: “It was mentioned to us that a man was on a road in Madinah when a woman passed by him. He followed her gaze until he came to a wall and his face was wounded. He came to the Prophet of God while his face was flowing with blood and said: O Prophet of God, I did such and such. The Prophet of God said to him: When God the Almighty intends to honor a servant, He hastens his punishment for his sin in this world, and when He intends to humiliate a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets him on the Day of Resurrection as if he were a tailless donkey.”

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of it.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it as and shall We reward with a ya and opened the zay as if the subject was not named, except the ungrateful in the nominative case.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as and shall We reward with a noon and with a kasra on the zay “except the ungrateful” in the accusative case.
The correct statement about this is that they are two well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one recites it, the reciter is correct.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of His blessings that He bestowed upon these people who wronged themselves: And We placed between their land and the towns which We had blessed, which are the Levant, towns visible. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The towns which We have blessed
, he said: Ash-Sham.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed
meaning the Levant.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
The towns which We have blessed
, he said: the Levant. It was said: It refers to the villages in which the Holy House was blessed.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed

, towns visible. He said: The land which We had blessed is the Holy Land. And His saying, towns visible, means: connected towns, and they are Arab towns. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja', he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan, regarding His statement,
h
And We placed between them and the towns which We have blessed

, towns visible, he said: Towns that were connected. He said: One of them would go out in the morning and take a nap in one town, and in the evening he would take shelter in another town. He said: A woman would place her basket on her head, then spin her spindle, and not come back until it was full of all the fruits.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Apparent villages means continuous.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, visible villages means: Arab villages between Medina and the Levant.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, villages visible, he said: the Sarawat.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, villages apparent, meaning: Arab villages, and they are between Medina and Ash-Sham.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed

, towns visible, he said: There were towns visible between their town and Ash-Sham. He said: A woman would go out with her spindle and her axe on her head, going from one town to the next, and she would be seen in a town carrying neither provisions nor water because of the distance between her and Ash-Sham. And His statement,
h
And We have determined therein the journey
, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And We have made between their towns and
h
the towns which We have blessed

a measured journey, from house to house, and from town to town. They do not stop except in one town, and they do not go out except from one town. And His saying, Travel therein, nights and days, in security. He says: And We said to them, Travel in these towns, between your towns and
h
the towns which We have blessed
, nights and days, in security, not fearing hunger or thirst, nor injustice from anyone. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “Travel therein in peace by night and by day,” they do not fear injustice or hunger, but they go out in the morning and take a nap, and they come back in the evening and spend the night in a village of people with a garden and a river, until it was mentioned to us that a woman would put her basket on her head and scoop it with her hand, and her basket would be full of fruit before she returned to her family without her having picked anything, and a man would travel without carrying with him provisions or a water skin from what had been spread out for the people.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and days of security, he said: There is no fear in them.

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement "Our Lord, extend between our journeys. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a supplication and a question with the letter alif.
Some of the people of Mecca and Basra read it as "ba'd" with a shaddah on the 'ayn as a supplication as well.

c: It was reported from the earlier scholars
m: that they used to read it as "Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a statement from God that God did that to them.

c: It was reported from another
m: that he read it as "Our Lord, ba'd" as a statement as well, except that the Lord is the vocative. The correct reading for this according to us is Our Lord, keep away and after because these are the two readings known in the reading of the regions, and what is other than them is not known among them. However, the interpretation of the people of interpretation also confirms the reading of the one who reads it as a supplication and a question, and this also increases the other reading’s distance from correctness. If this is the correct reading, then the interpretation of the statement is: “They said: O our Lord, extend our journeys, and place between us and Syria deserts and wildernesses, so that we may ride our camels therein and take provisions with us therein.” This is evidence of the people’s arrogance towards God’s blessing and kindness to them, and their ignorance of the extent of well-being. Their Lord hastened the answer to them, just as He hastened to those who said: If this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. He gave them what they desired and asked for from the question. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And they said

, ‘Our Lord, extend between our journeys.’ He said: They had villages connected to Yemen, some of which looked towards others, so they became arrogant about that and said: Our Lord, extend between our journeys. He said: So God sent upon them the flood of the dam, and made their food tamarisk, khutmah, and some few lote trees.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys.’ And they wronged themselves. He said: For they were arrogant in their lives and said, If the fruit of our gardens were further away than they are, it would be more fitting for us to desire it. So they were torn between Ash-Sham and Saba’ and their two gardens were exchanged for two gardens of bitter fruit and tamarisk, and some few lote trees.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And they said
, ‘Our Lord, lengthen our journeys.’ The people were insolent towards God’s blessings and disregarded God’s honor. God said, And they wronged themselves, so We made them [mere] stories.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘Our Lord, lengthen between our journeys,’ until we spend the night in the floe and in the deserts, and they wronged themselves, and His statement, and they wronged themselves, and their wronging of themselves was their doing what angered God with them of sins, which would necessitate God’s punishment for them, so We made them stories, he says: We made them stories for the people to use as an example of cursing, so it is said: The people dispersed like hands of cursing, and the hands of cursing if they dispersed and were cut off. And his saying, And We tore them apart in every way, means: And We dispersed them throughout the land in every way.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they wronged themselves, so We made them stories and tore them apart. Qatada said: Aamer Al-Sha’bi said: As for Ghassan, they went to Ash-Sham, and as for the Ansar, they went to Yathrib, and as for Khuza’a, they went to Tihama, and as for Azd, they went to Oman. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated from Ibn Ishaq: They claim that Imran ibn Amir, the paternal uncle of the people, was a soothsayer. He saw through his soothsaying that his people would be torn apart and scattered. So he said to them: “I know that you will be torn apart. So whoever among you has a long-term ambition, a strong camel, and new water bags, let him join a cup or a bag.” That was Wadih ibn Amr. And whoever among you has a city-dwelling ambition and is stubborn, let him join the land of Shan, that was Awf ibn Amr. They are the ones called Bariq. And whoever among you desires a secure life and a safe sanctuary, Surat Saba 34:19 Then they said, "Our Lord, lengthen our journeys." And they wronged themselves. So We made them stories and dispersed them in complete dispersion. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. let him join Al-Arzin, that was Khuza’a. And whoever desires lands firmly planted in the mud and nourished in a place, let him join Yathrib with its palm trees, that was Aws and Khazraj. So these are these two clans of the Ansar.” And whoever wants wine and yeast, gold and silk, and kingship and leadership, let him go to Kufa and Busra, for the Ghassanids, the sons of Jafna, were the kings of the Levant and those of them in Iraq. Ibn Ishaq said: I heard some of the people of knowledge say: This saying was said by the strange wife of Imran bin Amir, who was a soothsayer, and she saw that in her soothsaying, and God knows best which one it was. He said: So when they dispersed, they went to the soothsayer of Imran bin Amir. And His statement, Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person, God Almighty says: Indeed in Our tearing them apart are signs, meaning: a lesson, a warning, and an indication of the duty of God over His servant to be grateful for His blessings when He bestows them upon him, and His right to be patient in the face of his trial when He tests him with a trial for every patient and grateful person for His blessings. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. Mutraf used to say: What a good servant is the patient and grateful one who is given something and is grateful, and when he is tested he is patient.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement "Our Lord, extend between our journeys.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a supplication and a question with the letter alif.
Some of the people of Mecca and Basra read it as "ba'd" with a shaddah on the 'ayn as a supplication as well.
It was reported from the earlier scholars that they used to read it as "Our Lord, extend between our journeys" as a statement from God that God did that to them.
It was reported from another that he read it as "Our Lord, ba'd" as a statement as well, except that the Lord is the vocative.

The correct reading for this according to us is Our Lord, keep away and after because these are the two readings known in the reading of the regions, and what is other than them is not known among them.

However, the interpretation of the people of interpretation also confirms the reading of the one who reads it as a supplication and a question, and this also increases the other reading’s distance from correctness.

If this is the correct reading, then the interpretation of the statement is: “They said: O our Lord, extend our journeys, and place between us and Syria deserts and wildernesses, so that we may ride our camels therein and take provisions with us therein.”

x: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And indeed, Iblis proved his assumption about them to be true. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as And indeed, he proved true with a shaddah on the dal from to believe, meaning that he said, assuming that and you will not find most of them grateful. And he said, Then, by Your might, I will surely mislead them all, * Except for Your chosen servants among them
r

. Then his assumption about them was proven true, so he made it happen through them and through their following him. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Basra read it as And indeed, he proved true with a light dal, meaning: And indeed, his assumption about them was proven true. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings. This is because Iblis believed what he thought about the unbelievers of the children of Adam, and what he thought about them was true when he said, Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful. (al-A’raf 7:17), and when he said, And I will mislead them and arouse in them false desires.
r
(An-Nisa’: 119)
… the verse.

The enemy of God said that, thinking that he would do that, not knowing it, so it became true because they followed him. So whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement according to the reading of those who read with emphasis on the dal is: And indeed, Iblis assumed concerning those whose two gardens We replaced with two gardens of bitter food, as a punishment from Us for them, an uncertain assumption. He knew that they would follow him and obey him in disobeying God, so his assumption was confirmed regarding them, by his seducing them, until they obeyed him and disobeyed their Lord, except for a group of believers in God, for they remained steadfast in obeying God and disobeying Iblis. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, he said: Amr bin Malik told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he read
h
And Satan proved true about them his assumption
with a shaddah, and he said: He assumed an assumption, so his assumption was proven true.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And Satan proved true about them his assumption
. He said: He assumed an assumption, so they followed his assumption. He said: Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And Satan proved true about them his assumption
, God said: It was nothing but an assumption he made, and God does not believe a liar, nor does He disbelieve a truthful person.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And Satan proved true about them his assumption

, he said: Have you seen those whom I have honored, favored, and glorified? You will not find most of them grateful. This was an assumption on his part without knowledge, so God said, So they followed him, except for a group of believers.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And indeed, Iblis proved his assumption about them to be true.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as And indeed, he proved true with a shaddah on the dal from to believe, meaning that he said, assuming that and you will not find most of them grateful.
The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Basra read it as And indeed, he proved true with a light dal, meaning: And indeed, his assumption about them was proven true.
So whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct.

If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement according to the reading of those who read with emphasis on the dal is: And indeed, Iblis assumed concerning those whose two gardens We replaced with two gardens of bitter food, as a punishment from Us for them, an uncertain assumption.

x: God Almighty says: And Iblis had no argument against these people whose characteristics he described, to mislead them, except by Our giving them power over them, so that Our party and our allies might know who believes in the Hereafter meaning: who believes in resurrection, reward, and punishment from him who is in doubt about it who is not certain of the Resurrection, and who does not believe in reward or punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And he had no authority over them, he said: Al-Hasan said: By God, he did not strike them with a stick, sword, or whip, except with desires and desires to which he called them. He said: Saʿid narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement,
h
Except that We may know who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it
, he said: It was only a test so that God might know the disbeliever from the believer. It was also said that what was meant by his statement,
h
Except that We may know who believes in the Hereafter
, was Except that We may know that it exists and is apparent so that he may deserve reward or punishment. And His statement,
h
And your Lord is Guardian over all things

, God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is Guardian over the deeds of these disbelievers in Him, and other than that of all things. Nothing of it escapes His knowledge, and He will reward all of them on the Day of Resurrection for what they earned in this world of good and evil.

x: God the Most High says: This is what We did to Our servants and those who obeyed Us: David and Solomon, to whom We bestowed blessings upon them that have no equal, when they were grateful to Us. And that is what We did to Sheba, to whom We did, when they were arrogant about Our blessings, denied Our messengers, and disbelieved in Our hands. So say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people, who deny Our blessings to themselves: O people whom you claim have a partner with God besides Him, ask them to do to you some of Our actions with those whose affair We have described, whether they bestow blessings or despair. If they are unable to do that, then know that you are nullifiers, because partnership in Lordship is neither valid nor permissible. Then He described those they invoke besides God, saying: They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, of good or evil, harm or benefit.

So how can someone who is like that be a god? And His statement, And they have no share in them, meaning, the Most High says: Nor do they, since they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, alone in His kingdom besides God, possess it in the manner of a partnership, because ownership of what is owned does not belong to its owner except in one of two ways: either divided or shared. He says: And their gods that they call upon besides God, they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, neither divided nor shared. So how can someone who is like this be a partner to the One who owns all of that? And His statement, And he has no helper among them, meaning: And God has no helper from among the gods that they call upon besides Him to create any of that, nor to preserve it, since they do not own any of it, divided or shared. So it is said: He is your partner because He helped even if He does not own any of it.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “Say, ‘Call upon those you claim besides God. They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor will they have in either of them any share.’” He says, God has no partner in the heavens or on the earth, nor has He from them from those they call upon besides God any supporter of any help.

x: God Almighty says: And the intercession of an intercessor will not benefit anyone for whom he intercedes, whoever the intercessor may be, unless he intercedes for someone for whom God has given permission to intercede. God Almighty says: So if intercessions do not benefit anyone with God except for someone for whom God has given permission to intercede, and God does not give permission to any of His friends to intercede for anyone of the disbelievers in Him, and you are people of disbelief in Him, O polytheists. So how can you worship someone you worship instead of God, claiming that you worship him so that he may bring you closer to God and intercede for you with your Lord? So whoever since this is the meaning of the words in His statement except for someone for whom He has given permission: the one for whom intercession is made. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase he gave him permission.
The majority of reciters read it with a damma on the alif of he gave him permission as if the agent was not named.

Some of the Kufians read it as he gave him permission with a difference of opinion about it, meaning God gave him permission. And his saying, until fear is removed from their hearts, means: until fear is removed from their hearts, and it goes away. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, until fear is removed from their hearts, means: it is removed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Until fear is removed from their hearts, he said: The cover is removed from them on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When it is revealed from their hearts. The commentators differed regarding who those described with this attribute are and the reason for their hearts being frightened.

x: Some of them said: Those whose hearts are frightened are the angels. They said: Their hearts are only frightened by the faintness that befalls them when they hear God’s revelation.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Ibn Mas’ud said
m: regarding this verse, Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, he said: When something happens to the Lord of the Throne, the angels below him hear a sound like the dragging of a chain on a rock, and they faint. Then, when the fear has departed from their hearts, they call out to one another, What has your Lord said? He said: He says: Whoever He wills. He says: The Truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Al-Mu'tamir told us:
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Masruq, who said: When something happens in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, the angels hear a sound like a chain being dragged on a rock. He said: Then they faint, and when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say? He said: Then He says: Whoever God wills, the Truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, that he said:
m: When a matter occurs to the Lord of the Throne, then he mentioned a similar meaning except that he said: They are overcome by fear, until when that has gone from them they call out to one another: What did your Lord say?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud,
m: regarding His statement,
h
until fear is banished from their hearts

, he said: When the revelation is given, the inhabitants of the heavens hear a clanging like the clanging of a chain on a rock. He said: Then they call out to each other in the heavens, What has your Lord said? He said: Then they call out to each other, The Truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. And on his authority, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, who said:
m: “The command descends from the Lord of Majesty to the lowest heaven, and the people of the lowest heaven are terrified until the command concerning which it was revealed becomes clear to them. Then some of them say to one another: What did your Lord say? They say: The truth has been said, and He is the Most High, the Grand. This is what He says: ‘
h
Until fear is banished from their hearts
’... the verse.”

c: Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dhabi told us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Abu Hurayrah told us, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings together, and there is a sound like the sound of a chain on a rocky plain. This is what He said: ‘Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, “What has your Lord said?” They say, “The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand.”’”

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, he said:
m: “Al-Harith ibn Hisham said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘How does revelation come to you?’ He said: ‘It comes to me in a ringing sound like the ringing of a bell, and then it leaves me when it leaves me and I have memorized it. And sometimes it comes in the form of a man, and speaks to me in words, and that is easier for me.’”

c: Zakariya ibn Abaan al-Masri told me: Na'im told us: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zakariya, on the authority of Jabir ibn Haywah, on the authority of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God wants to reveal something, He speaks the revelation, and the heavens tremble, or he said, a violent tremor, out of fear of God's command. When the inhabitants of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall down in prostration to God. The first to raise his head is Gabriel, and God speaks to him from His revelation what He wills. Then Gabriel passes by the angels. Every time he passes by a heaven, the angels ask him: 'What did our Lord say, O Gabriel?' Gabriel says: 'The Truth said, and He is the Most High, the Grand.' They all say the same as Gabriel said, and Gabriel ends with the revelation where God has commanded him."

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Until, when fear has been banished from their hearts… the verse. He said: Ibn Abbas used to say: “When God wanted to reveal to Muhammad, He called Gabriel. When our Lord spoke with the revelation, his voice was like the sound of iron on a rock. When the inhabitants of the heavens heard the sound of iron, they fell down in prostration. When Gabriel brought them the message, they raised their heads and said, ‘What has your Lord said?’ They said, ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ And this is the saying of the angels.”

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Until, when fear has been banished from their hearts… to And He is the Most High, the Grand, he said: When God, the Most High, revealed to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, He called the Messenger from the angels and sent him with the revelation. The angels heard the voice of the Almighty speaking with the revelation. When He uncovered their hearts, they asked about what God had said, and they said, The truth, and they knew that God only says the truth, and that He will fulfill what He promised. Ibn Abbas said: The sound of the revelation was like the sound of iron on a rock. When they heard it, they fell down in prostration. When they raised their heads, they said, What has your Lord said? They said, “The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand.” Then God commanded His Prophet to ask the people, Say, ‘Who provides for you from the heavens?’… to His statement, In manifest error.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim,
m: regarding His statement, Until, when fear has been banished from their hearts... the verse, he said: The revelation descends from the sky, and when He fulfills it, “They will say, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They will say, ‘The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
until fear is banished from their hearts

, he said: When the revelation is decreed in the corners of the heavens, he said: Like the sound of steel striking a rock. He said: They become fearful, not knowing what has happened, so they become frightened. Then when the messengers pass by them, “They say, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say, ‘The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand.’”

x: Others, who said: Those described with this are the angels, said: What is frightening to their hearts is their fear of God’s decree that He decrees, out of fear that it will be the Day of Resurrection.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Until, when fear has been removed from their hearts, they say, ‘What did your Lord say?’… the verse. He said: God inspires Gabriel, and the angels disperse, or are frightened out of fear that it is something of the Hour. Then, when it is removed from their hearts and they know that it is not of the Hour, “They say, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They say, ‘The truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand.’”

x: Others said: Rather, this is the action of the angels of the heavens when the angels pass by them, fearing that the Hour has happened. Surat Saba 34:23 And no intercession will benefit with Him except for him whom He permits until, when fear is banished from their hearts, they say, "What did your Lord say?" They say, "The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand."
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
Until fear is banished from their hearts

… the verse, Ibn Mas’ud claimed that the angels who follow one another to the earth record their deeds. When the Lord sends them and they descend, a loud sound is heard from them, and those of the angels who are below them think that it is from the matter of the Hour, so they fall down in prostration. And so it is whenever they pass by them that they do that out of fear of their Lord.

x: Others said: Rather, those described with this are the polytheists. They said: Rather, Satan is frightened of their hearts. He said: Rather, they say: What did your Lord say when death descended upon them?
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Until fear is banished from their hearts

, he said: Satan is banished from their hearts and departs from them and their hopes, and from what used to lead them astray. They said, ‘What did your Lord say?’ They said, ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ He said: This is regarding the children of Adam, and this is at death, when they acknowledge it when acknowledgment does not benefit them. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one reported by Al-Sha'bi on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, due to the authenticity of the report we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which supports it. Since this is the case, the meaning of the statement is: Intercession with Him will not benefit anyone except for the one whom He has given permission to intercede with Him. So when God gives permission to the one whom He has given permission to intercede, he will be terrified by hearing His permission, until when the fear has left their hearts, and is removed from them, and the fear has been removed from them, they will say: What did your Lord say? The angels said: The Truth, And He is the Most High over all things, The Great, to whom nothing is below. The Arabs use the word fazza in two meanings. They say of the brave man who is subject to the matters that frighten him: huwa mufazza' he is a frightened man, and they say of the coward who is frightened by everything: in fact he is a frightened man. Likewise, they say of the man in whose favor people decide matters by dominating the one who disputes with him: huwa mughlib he is a conqueror, and if this meaning is intended, then he is victorious. They also say of the man who is forever defeated: mughlib he is a conqueror. The reciters differed in their recitation of this verse. The majority of reciters in all regions recited it as fāz’a with a zay and an ‘ayn, based on the interpretation we mentioned from Ibn Mas’ud and those who shared his opinion on this.

c: It was narrated from Al-Hasan
m: that he recited it as until when he was free from their hearts with a ra’ and a ghayn, based on the interpretation we mentioned from Ibn Zayd. It may be possible that the meaning of Al-Hasan’s recitation of this verse could be interpreted as until when he was free from their hearts so they became empty of the fear that had befallen them.

c: It was narrated from Mujahid
m: that he recited it as fāz’a meaning: God removed the fear from them. The correct reading in this regard is with the letters zay and ayn, due to the consensus of the jurists among the reciters and interpreters of the Qur’an on this, and due to the authenticity of the report that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supporting it and indicating its authenticity.
