The majority of reciters read it with a damma on the alif of he gave him permission as if the agent was not named.
Some of the Kufians read it as he gave him permission with a difference of opinion about it, meaning God gave him permission.

Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amir told us, he said: Qurra told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim, regarding His statement, Until, when fear has been banished from their hearts... the verse, he said: The revelation descends from the sky, and when He fulfills it, “They will say, ‘What did your Lord say?’
The reciters differed in their recitation of this verse.
The majority of reciters in all regions recited it as fāz’a with a zay and an ‘ayn, based on the interpretation we mentioned from Ibn Mas’ud and those who shared his opinion on this.
It was narrated from Al-Hasan that he recited it as until when he was free from their hearts with a ra’ and a ghayn, based on the interpretation we mentioned from Ibn Zayd.
It was narrated from Mujahid that he recited it as fāz’a meaning: God removed the fear from them.

The correct reading in this regard is with the letters zay and ayn, due to the consensus of the jurists among the reciters and interpreters of the Qur’an on this, and due to the authenticity of the report that we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supporting it and indicating its authenticity.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate idols and statues with their Lord: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth by sending down rain upon you from it as life for your crops and improvement for your livelihoods, and by subjecting the sun, the moon, and the stars for your benefits and as sources of your sustenance, and the earth by bringing forth from it your sustenance and the sustenance of your livestock? And He left out the information about the people’s answer, sufficing with the evidence of the speech on it, then He mentioned it, which is: If they say: We do not know, then say: The one who provides for you is God, and either we or you, O people, are upon guidance or in manifest error. He says: Say to them: We are upon guidance or in error, or you are upon error or on guidance.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Say: ‘Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?’ Say: ‘God.’ And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error.” He said: The companions of Muhammad said that to the polytheists: “By God, you and I are not on the same path. Indeed, one of the two groups is guided.” And some people said: The meaning of that is: Indeed, we are upon right guidance, and indeed, you are in manifest error.”

x: Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Shaheedi told me: Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah and Ziyad,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And either we or you are upon guidance or in manifest error
, he said: We are upon guidance, and you are in manifest error. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of or in this position.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is not because of doubt, but this is in the speech of the Arabs as if he is the one who is guided. He said: A man may say to his slave: One of us is hitting his companion, and there is no problem for the listener that the master is the one hitting. Another of them said: The meaning of this is: We are on the right path, and you are in clear error, because the Arabs place or in the place of the waw of connection. Jarir said: Ath’alaba of the knights or winds that have changed them, Tahya and Al-Khashab He said: He means Tha’laba and Rayyah. He said: This was said by someone who had no doubt in his religion, and they knew that they were on the right path, and those were in error. So it is said: This, even though it was a single statement in mockery, he said this to them, and he said: If their love is right, I will follow it, and I am not mistaken if it is wrong.

Some of the people of Kufa said: The meaning of or and the meaning of and in this place is the same, except that the evidence for something else is not or in the place of and, but it is in the delegated matter, as you say: If you wish, take a dirham or two, then he can take two or one, but he does not have the right to take three. He said: And it is according to the opinion of those who do not understand Arabic, and they make or in the place of and, and it is permissible for him to take three, because in their saying it is like your saying: Take a dirham or two. He said: The meaning of we or you is that we are astray or guided, and you are also astray, and he knows that his Messenger is the guided one, and that others are astray. He said: And you say in speech to a man who accuses you of lying: By God, one of us is a liar, and you mean him, and you lied to him with an undisclosed lie. And this is found in the Qur’an and the speech of the Arabs a lot, to direct speech to its best paths, if it is known, like what a speaker says to someone who says: By God, so-and-so has arrived, and he is a liar, so he says: Say: God willing, or say: I think so, so he lies to him with the best explicit lie.

He said: And from the speech of the Arabs is to say: May God kill him, then it is ugly and they say: May God kill him, and may God smite him. He said: And from that are: Woe to you, and woe to you, they are in the meaning of: Woe to you, except that they are less than it. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that it is a command from God to His Prophet to refute the one who ordered him to address him with this statement with the most beautiful refutation, just as a man says to a friend of his who is addressing him, and he wants to refute him in a piece of report he has: One of us is a liar. The one who said that means his friend, not himself, and for this reason the speech was made with or.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say to these polytheists: One of our party is upon guidance and the other is astray. You will not be asked about the crimes we committed and the sins we committed, nor will we be asked about the deeds you do. Say to them: Our Lord will gather us together before Him on the Day of Resurrection, then He will judge between us with truth. He says: Then He will judge between us with justice, and at that time it will be distinguished from the one who is guided among us who is astray. And He is the Opener, the Knowing. He says: God is the Judge, the All-Knowing of judgment between His creation, because nothing is hidden from Him, and He does not need witnesses to know who is right from who is wrong. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “Say: Our Lord will gather us together” on the Day of Resurrection, then He will judge between us: that is, He will judge between us.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, And He is the Opener, the All-Knowing, meaning: the Judge.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate gods and idols with God: Show me, O people whom you have associated with God and made them partners with Him in your worship of them: What have they created on earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? No! God Almighty says: They lied. The matter is not as they described, nor as they made and said, that God has a partner. Rather, He is the worshipped One who has no partner, and it is not fitting that He should have a partner in His kingdom. He is the Mighty in His vengeance upon those of His creation who associate partners with Him, the Wise in His management of His creation.

God Almighty says: We did not send you, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people specifically, but We sent you to all of mankind, Arabs and non-Arabs, red and black, as a bringer of good tidings to those who obey you, and a warner to those who deny you. But most people do not know that God sent you thus to all of humanity. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We have not sent you except as a mercy to mankind

, he said: God sent Muhammad to the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and God honored them for him. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the forerunner of the Arabs, Suhaib is the forerunner of the Romans, Bilal is the forerunner of the Abyssinians, and Salman is the forerunner of the Persians.

x: God Almighty says: And these polytheists say when they hear God’s threat to the unbelievers and what He will do to them in their place of resurrection from what God has revealed in His Book, When will this promise come? and at what time will it be if you are truthful in what you promise us of that, that it will come to pass.

God said to His Prophet: Say to them, O Muhammad, “for you, O people, is an appointed time for a Day that will come to you. Do not delay it when it comes to you, when an hour comes to you, so look to repentance and turning back, and do not anticipate” it with punishment, because God has set a term for that for you.
God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved from the polytheists of the Arabs said,
h
We will not believe in this Qur’an
that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to us, nor in the book that others brought before him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We will not believe in this Qur’an
, nor in that which was before it, he said: The polytheists said:
h
We will not believe in this Qur’an
, nor in that which was before it of books and prophets. And His saying,
h
And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord

, blaming each other, arguing with each other. The oppressed ones in this world will say to those who were arrogant towards them in it: If it were not for you, the leaders and the great ones in this world, we would have believed in God and His signs.

x: God Almighty says, Those who were arrogant in this world, so they led in misguidance and disbelief in God, said to those who were oppressed in it, so they were followers of the people of misguidance among them, when they said to them, Had it not been for you, we would have been believers: Did we turn you away from guidance and prevent you from following the truth after it had come to you from God, making it clear to you? Rather, you were criminals. So your preference for disbelief in God over faith prevented you from following guidance and believing in God and His Messenger.

God Almighty says, And those who were oppressed said of the disbelievers in God in this world, so they were followers of their leaders in misguidance to those who were arrogant in it, so they were their leaders Rather, it is a plot “How much for us by night and day has it turned us away from guidance
h
when you command us to disbelieve in God
and make for Him examples and likenesses in worship and divinity, so the plot was attributed to the night and the day.

i: The meaning is what we mentioned of the plot of the arrogant against the oppressed by night and by day, despite the breadth of the Arabs in what has been known of its meaning from their language, from transferring the description of a thing to something else, so you say to a man: O so-and-so, your day is fasting and your night is standing, and as the poet said:
x: I slept, but the mounts were not asleep at night And what is similar to that which we have already explained in other places in this book of ours.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Rather, it was your plotting by night and by day when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals, he said, rather, it was your plotting against us by night and by day, O great leaders, until you removed us from the worship of God. It was mentioned in its interpretation on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair what:

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: Rather, the plotting of night and day. He said: The plotting of night and day. And his saying,
h
When you command us to disbelieve in God
, means:
h
When you command us to disbelieve in God
. And His saying, And We make for Him equals, means: partners.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And We will make for Him equals, meaning partners. His statement, And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, meaning: They will regret what they neglected in obeying God in this world when they saw the punishment of God that He had prepared for them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they kept their regret secret among themselves when they saw the punishment. His statement,
h
And We have placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved

, and the hands of those who disbelieved in God will be shackled to their necks in Hellfire, in recompense for their disbelief in God in this world. God Almighty says: God does not do this to them except as a reward for the evil deeds they did in this world, and as a recompense for them.

x: God Almighty says: And We did not send to the people of a city a warner, warning them that Our punishment would descend upon them because of their disobedience to Us, except that its leaders and chiefs said in error, as the polytheistic people of Pharaoh said to him: We are disbelievers in what you were sent with as a warner and what you were sent with of the Oneness of God, and disavowal of deities and rivals. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We did not send to any city a warner but its affluent ones said
, ‘Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.’ He said: They are their leaders and their chiefs in evil.

x: God Almighty says: And the people of arrogance against God from every city to which We sent a warner to Our prophets and messengers said: We are more in wealth and children, and we will not be punished in the Hereafter. Because if God had not been pleased with our religion and actions, He would not have given us wealth and children, nor would He have expanded our provision for us. Rather, He gave us what He gave us of that because He was pleased with our deeds, and He preferred us over others because of our superiority and our closeness to Him.

God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad, Indeed, my Lord expands provision of living and luxury in this world for whomever He wills of His creation and restricts it for whomever He wills, not out of love for the one for whom He expands it, nor any good in it or any favor that he deserves from Him, nor out of hatred from Him for the one over whom He restricts it, nor out of loathing, but rather He does that as a trial and trial for His servants. Most people do not know that God does that as a test for His servants, but they think that it is from Him out of love for the one for whom He expands it and hatred for the one over whom He restricts it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you closer to Us… the verse, he said: They said: We have more wealth and children, so God informed them that it is not your wealth and your children that bring you closer to Us, except for those who believe and do righteousness. He said: This is what the polytheists said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. They said: If God had not been pleased with us, He would not have given us this, just as Qarun said: If God had not been pleased with me and my condition, He would not have given me this. He said: Does he not know that God destroyed generations before him? (al-Qasas 28:78) to the end of the verse.

x: God Almighty says: What is your wealth that you boast about, O people, and what is your children that you act arrogantly with, that brings you closer to Us? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, With Us is nearness, he said: nearness.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you nearer to Us
, people do not consider the abundance of wealth and children, and the unbeliever may be given wealth, and it may be withheld from the believer. And He, the Most High, said,
h
And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you nearer to Us
, and He did not say both, and He mentioned wealth and children, and they are two different types because He mentioned a plural for each type that can be used to refer to which.

i: If someone said that He meant one of the two types, his statement would not be far-fetched, and that would be like the saying of the poet:
x: We are satisfied with what we have, and you are satisfied with what you have, and the opinion differs He did not say: satisfied.
And His statement,
h
Except for he who believes and does righteous deeds
, the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: It is not your wealth or your children that bring you closer to Us,
h
except for he who believes and does righteous deeds
. For their wealth and children bring them closer to Us through their obedience to God in that and their fulfillment of their right to Him in it, not the people of disbelief in God.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, he said: Their wealth and children will not harm them in this world for the believers. And he recited, For those who do good is the best [reward] and even more
r
(Yunus 10:26)

. So the best [reward] is Paradise, and the extra is what God gave them in this world for which He did not hold them accountable, as He held others accountable. So whoever interprets it in this way, it is an accusative case because of the occurrence of approach on it. And it may be possible that of is in the nominative case, so it is as if it was said: And it is only for those who believe and do righteous deeds. And His statement,
h
For them is a double reward
, means:
h
For them is a double reward
from God for their righteous deeds, eleven times. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
For those there is a double reward for what they did
, he said: For their eleven deeds, and in the way of God for one there are seven hundred. His saying,
h
In the chambers
, safe, means: They are
h
in the chambers
of Paradise, safe from the punishment of God.

x: God Almighty says: And those who act against Our verses, meaning: against Our proofs and the verses of Our Book, seeking to invalidate it and wanting to extinguish its light as helpers, thinking that they can outsmart Us and defeat Us. Those will be brought to the punishment, meaning they will be brought to the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

Say, 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants.' God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whomever He wills of His creation. He expands it for him as an honor to him or otherwise, and He restricts it for whomever He wills of them, making it tight and stingy, as an insult to him or otherwise, but rather as a trial and a test. 'And whatever you spend, He will replace it.'" He says: Whatever you spend, O people, in the obedience of God, God will replace it for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: And whatever you spend, He will replace it. He said: Whatever was neither extravagant nor miserly. And His saying,
h
And He is the Best of Providers
, means: He is the best of those who are said to provide and described with, because someone other than Him may be described with that, so it is said: So-and-so provides for his family and children.

x: God Almighty says: And on the Day We shall gather all these disbelievers in God, then We shall say to the angels: Did these worship you instead of Us? Then the angels shall disown them.

"They said, 'Glory be to You, our Lord, sanctifying You and disavowing what these have attributed to You of partners and rivals. You are our protector apart from them. We will not take a protector apart from You. Rather, they used to worship the jinn." And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And the Day He will gather them all together and then say to the angels, ‘Was it these that they used to worship?’ is a question, like His statement to Jesus, Did you tell the people to take me and my mother as deities besides God? (al-Ma’idah 5:116). His saying,
h
Most of them are believers in them
, means: Most of them believe in the jinn, claiming that they are the daughters of God. God is far above what they say, far above.

x: God Almighty says: “So today, O angels, some of you will not possess any benefit to benefit you or any harm to reach you or you to reach them. And We will say to those who did wrong,” meaning: And We will say to those who worshipped other than God, placing worship in the wrong place and making it for someone other than the one for whom it should be, Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny, in this world. You have already reached it.

God the Almighty says: And when the verses of Our Book are recited to these polytheists as clear proofs: He says: Clear that they are the truth from Us, They say, ‘This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.’ He says: They said at that time: Do not follow Muhammad, for he is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship of idols, and to change your religion and the religion of your fathers. And they say, ‘This is nothing but a fabricated lie.’ God the Almighty says: And these polytheists say: What is this that you recite to us, O Muhammad, meaning the Qur’an, is nothing but a lie. He says: Except a fabricated lie: He says: Invented, conjectured. And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, ‘This is not but obvious magic.’ God Almighty says: And the disbelievers said of the truth, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when it came to them, meaning: when God sent him as a prophet: This is not but obvious magic: He says: This is not but obvious magic, making it clear to whoever saw it and contemplated it that it was magic.

God Almighty says: And We did not send down upon the polytheists who said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he came to them with Our signs: This is obvious magic - what they say of that - books which they study: meaning, they read them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We did not give them any books to study means that they read them

, And We did not send to them before you any warner means: And We did not send to these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, regarding what they say and do before you, any prophet to warn them of Our punishment upon them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We did not send to them before you any warner. God did not send down a book to the Arabs before the Qur’an, nor did He send to them a prophet before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: And We did not send down upon the polytheists who said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he came to them with Our signs: This is obvious magic - what they say of that - books which they study: meaning, they read them.

As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We did not give them any books to study means that they read them, And We did not send to them before you any warner means: And We did not send to these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, regarding what they say and do before you, any prophet to warn them of Our punishment upon them.

x: And His statement,
h
And those before them denied

, means: And those before them of the nations denied Our messengers and Our revelation. And they did not attain a tenth of what We gave them, means: And your people, O Muhammad, did not attain a tenth of what We gave those before them of the nations of power, strength, and might, and other blessings. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they have not attained a tenth of what We have given them of strength in this world

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And they have not attained even a tenth of what We have given them
, meaning: They have not exceeded a tenth of what We have bestowed upon them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And those before them denied
, and they did not attain a tenth of what We gave them, informs you that He gave the people what they were not given of strength and other things.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they have not attained even a tenth of what We gave them

, he said: These people, the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, have not attained even a tenth of what We gave those before them, nor what We gave them of this world, nor what We extended to them. So they denied My messengers, so how was My reproach? He says: So they denied My messengers in what they brought them of My message, so We punished them by changing for them what We had given them of blessings. So look, O Muhammad, how was My reproach. He says: How was My changing and My punishment for them.

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your al-Nas 114:I only admonish you, O people, with one thing, which is obedience to God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
I only admonish you of one thing
, he said: Obedience to God. His saying,
h
That you stand up for God in pairs and individually

, means: And that one thing that I advise you with is that you stand up for God in pairs, and and individually individually, so an is in the accusative case, translating it as one. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told me, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, That you stand before God in pairs and individually, he said: One and two.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, “Say, ‘
h
I only admonish you of one thing
: that you stand up for God in pairs and singly’” - one man and two men. It was also said that it was said,
h
I only admonish you of one thing

, and that one thing is that you stand up for God by giving sincere advice and abandoning desires. In pairs means: A man among you stands up with another and they engage in a friendly debate, “Have you ever known Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to be insane?” Then each one of you stands aside and thinks and considers individually whether that was the case with him, so you will know then that he is a warner to you. His statement,
h
Then consider that your companion is not mad
, means that he is not crazy. His statement,
h
He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment

, means that Muhammad is only a warner who warns you of his punishment for your disbelief in God before the punishment of Hell before you reach it. His statement, He, is a metaphor for the name Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to your people who deny you, who reject what you have brought them from your Lord: I do not ask you for compensation for warning you of God’s punishment, frightening you with His wrath, and advising you in my command to you to believe in God and know how to obey Him. It is for you, I have no need of it. Rather, the meaning of the words is: Say to them: I did not ask you for compensation for that, lest you accuse me and think that I only called you to follow what I take from you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “Say: I have not asked you for any reward” means any reward for it is yours meaning: I have not asked you for any reward for Islam. His statement,
h
My reward is only from God

, means: What is my reward for calling you to believe in God, to know how to obey Him, and to convey His message to you, except from God? And He is Witness over all things, meaning: God is Witness over the truth of what I say to you, and He bears witness to it for me, and to all other things.

x: The Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, Indeed, my Lord casts the truth, which is the revelation. He says: He sends it down from the sky, and casts it to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Knower of the unseen, He says: Knower of what is hidden from sight, and has no manifestation, and what has not been of what is to come. This is from the attributes of the Lord, except that it is raised because it comes after the predicate. And this is what the Arabs do when the description comes after the predicate, in that they follow the description with the syntactic analysis of what is in the predicate, so they say: Indeed, your father stands up, the generous. So the generous is raised as described, and the accusative is permissible in it, because it is an attribute of the father, so its syntactic analysis is followed.

"Say: The truth has come." He says: Say to them, O Muhammad: The Qur'an and the revelation of God have come. And falsehood does not originate. He says: And falsehood does not create creation. Falsehood, as the people of interpretation have explained, is Satan. And it does not bring him back. He says: Nor does it bring him back to life after his annihilation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “Say: My Lord casts the truth”: meaning the revelation. “Knower of the unseen. Say: The truth has come”: meaning the Qur’an. And falsehood does not originate, nor does it restore: falsehood is Satan, meaning Satan does not create anyone, nor does he resurrect him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord casts the truth upon falsehood, Knower of the unseen,’ and he recited, Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 18)
… until His statement, And for you is woe for that which you describe
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 18)

, he said: God destroys falsehood and confirms the truth with which He stamped falsehood, He stamps the truth upon falsehood, so falsehood is destroyed and the truth is confirmed. That is His statement, Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord casts the truth upon falsehood, Knower of the unseen.’

x: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to your al-Nas 114:If I have strayed from guidance and taken a path other than the right path, then my straying from the right path is only to my own detriment. He says: My straying from guidance is to my own detriment. And if I am guided He says: And if I remain steadfast on the truth. Then it is by what my Lord reveals to me He says: Then it is by the revelation of God that He reveals to me, and His success in steadfastness on the path of truth and the path of guidance. And His statement, He is All-Hearing, All-Near, means: My Lord has heard what I say to you, preserved it, and He will reward me for my truthfulness in that, and that is not far from me, so it is difficult for Him to hear what I say to you, what you say, and what others say. But He is close to every speaker, hearing everything he utters, closer to him than the jugular vein.
God Almighty says to the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you could but see, O Muhammad,
h
when they are terrified
. The commentators differed about the meanings of this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to these polytheists whom God Almighty described in His saying: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, ‘This is not but a man who wants to avert you from what your fathers used to worship.’ He said: What is meant by His saying:
h
When they are terrified
, there is no escape, and they are seized from a nearby place is when God’s punishment descends upon them in this world.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, there is no escape ... to the end of the verse, he said: This is from the torment of this world.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And they were seized from a nearby place
, that this is the torment of this world.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified

, there is no escape… to the end of the surah, he said: These are the polytheists from the people of Badr, this verse was revealed about them. He said: They are the ones who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief, and made their people dwell in the abode of destruction, Hell, the people of Badr from the polytheists.

x: Others said: He meant that they would be swallowed up by a deserted land.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, there is no escape, he said: They are the army that will be swallowed up by the earth in the desert, and one man will remain among them to inform the people of what happened to his companions.

c: Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: Sufyan bin Saeed narrated to us, he said: Mansur bin Al Mu’tamir narrated to me, on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash, he said:
m: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman say: “The Messenger of God said, and he mentioned a tribulation that will occur between the people of the East and the West. He said: While they are like that, the Sufyani will emerge from the dry valley in a state of turmoil until he descends upon Damascus. He will send two armies: an army to the East, and an army to Medina, until they descend upon the land of Babylon, in the cursed city and the wicked spot. They will kill more than three thousand, and slaughter there more than one hundred women, and kill there three hundred rams from the Abbasids. Then they will descend to Kufa and destroy what is around it. Then they will go out heading towards Ash-Sham. The banner of this one will emerge from Kufa, and that army will overtake it against the two groups, and they will kill them. No one will escape from them, and they will rescue what is in their hands of captives and spoils, and his next army will evacuate Medina. They will plunder it for three days and nights, then they will leave, heading for Mecca. When they are in the desert, God will send Gabriel, who will say: “O Gabriel, go and destroy them.” He will strike it with his foot, a blow that will cause the earth to swallow them up. This is what He said in Surat Saba’:
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, there is no escape… the verse. None of them will escape except two men: one of them will be a bearer of good tidings, and the other a warner, and they are from Juhayna.” Therefore, the saying came:

c: And the report is certain with Juhayna Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told us:
m: I asked Rawad ibn al-Jarrah about the hadith that he narrated on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rib’i, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about a story he mentioned in the Fitnah. He said: So I said to him: Tell me about this hadith that you heard from Sufyan al-Thawri? He said: No. I said: Did you recite it to him? He said: No. I said: Was it recited to him while you were present? He said: No. I said: What is its story, what is its report? He said: Some people came to me and said: We have with us a strange hadith, or some words to this effect, we recite it and you hear it. I said to them: Bring it. So they recited it to me, then they went and narrated it from me, or words to this effect.
b.via: the report is certain with Juhayna Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani

c: Muhammad ibn Khalaf told me
m: some of this hadith. He said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rib’i, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was a long hadith. He said: I saw it in the book of al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of Rawad, on the authority of Surat Saba 34:51
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, but there is no escape, and they are seized from a place nearby. Sufyan in full.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the polytheists when they were frightened when they came out of their graves.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: his statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, he said: They will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection when they emerge from their graves. Qatada said:
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, but there is no escape, and they are seized from a nearby place when they witness God’s punishment.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Ma’qil:
m: h
And if you could but see when they are terrified

, there is no escape. He said: He terrified them on the Day of Resurrection, but they did not escape. What is more correct in interpreting this, and more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the statement of those who said: “God’s threat to the polytheists who disbelieved in the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from his people” because the verses before this verse came to inform about them and their reasons, and about God’s threat to them of His consequences, and this verse is in the context of those verses, so it is more likely for it to be a report about their condition than a report about something that was not mentioned. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, these polytheists from your people, and witness them
h
when they are terrified
at witnessing God’s punishment, “there is no escape meaning there is no way then for them to escape themselves, or to outrun Us by fleeing, and escape from Our punishment.

c: As Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, there is no escape, meaning: there is no escape.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if you could but see when they are terrified
, there is no escape, he said: There is no escape. His saying,
h
And they were seized from a nearby place
, means: And God seized them with His punishment from a nearby place, because since they were close to God, they were not far from Him.

evidence.text: He said: No. I said: Did you recite it to him?
He said: Some people came to me and said: We have with us a strange hadith, or some words to this effect, we recite it and you hear it.
So they recited it to me, then they went and narrated it from me, or words to this effect.

x: God Almighty says: And these polytheists said when they saw the punishment of God, We believe in it, meaning: We believe in God, His Book, and His Messenger. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And they said
, ‘We believe in him,’ they said: We believe in God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they said
, ‘We believe in it,’ at that time, meaning: when they witnessed God’s punishment. Yunus narrated, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they said
, ‘We believe in him,’ after the killing. And His statement,
h
And how can they fight

? He said: From what point of view can they fight? The readers of the cities differed on this. The majority of the readers of Medina read it as tanawush without a hamza, meaning: to take, and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it as tanawush with a hamza, meaning: tanawush, which is to slow down. It is said from it: tanawasht al-shay’: I took it from far away, and nashta: I took it from close by. From tanawush, the poet said: Naish wished he had obeyed me, but things happened after that. And from the Nosh is the saying of the rajaz poet: It rushes into the basin from a height, rushing through it, crossing the desert. In war, when some of them approached each other with spears but did not meet, it is said: The people have skirmished. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings known among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning. That is because the meaning of that is:
h
And they said

, We believe in God, while what they said did not benefit them. So God said, And how can they reach an agreement? That is, where can they reach repentance and return? That is, they have become far from them, so they have become like a place far from which they can reach it. And that place was described as far away because they said that on the Day of Resurrection, so God said, How can they reach an agreement? And the accepted repentance was only in this world, and this world has gone and become far from the Hereafter. So whichever of the two readings you mentioned the reciter recites, then he is correct in that. It may be possible that those who read it with a hamza used a hamza, and they intended the meaning of someone who did not use a hamza, but they used a hamza because of the addition of the waw, so they changed it, as was said And when the messengers were fed (al-Mursalat 77:11), so the waw was made from waqtat, since it was a damma, they used a hamza. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Atiyah told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, he said:
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: What do you think of the statement of God, And how can they come to terms with each other? He said: They ask for a response, but there is no time for a response.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And how can they fight
? means: How can they respond?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And how can they fight
? He said: The response.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us,
m: And how can they approach? He said: from a far place.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘We believe in him,’ but how can they seize him from a distant place? He said: These are the dead of the people of Badr, those of them who were killed. And he recited, And if you could but see when they are terrified and there is no escape, and they are seized from a place nearby, and they say, ‘We believe in him,’… the verse. He said: Seizing means grasping, and how can they attain repentance from a distant place, when they have abandoned it in this world? He said: This is after death in the Hereafter. He said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement,
h
And they said
, ‘We believe in him,’ after the killing, And how can they attack him from a distant place? And he recited, Nor those who die while they are disbelievers
r
(An-Nisa’: 18)

. He said: They have no repentance. He said: God offered them to repent once, and God would accept it from them, but they refused, or they offer repentance after death. He said: So they offer it in the Hereafter five times, and God would refuse to accept it from them. He said: And the one who repents at death has no repentance. And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord!’ (al-An’am 6:27)... the verse. And he recited, “Our Lord, we have seen and we have heard, so return us [to the world]; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” (al-Sajdah 32:12).

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And how can they fight
? He said: And how can they return? His saying, from a far place, means: from their afterlife to this world.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, from a distant place from the Hereafter to this world.

evidence.text: The readers of the cities differed on this.

The majority of the readers of Medina read it as tanawush without a hamza, meaning: to take, and the majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it as tanawush with a hamza, meaning: tanawush, which is to slow down.
The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings known among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning.
So whichever of the two readings you mentioned the reciter recites, then he is correct in that.

It may be possible that those who read it with a hamza used a hamza, and they intended the meaning of someone who did not use a hamza, but they used a hamza because of the addition of the waw, so they changed it, as was said And when the messengers were fed (al-Mursalat 77:11), so the waw was made from waqtat, since it was a damma, they used a hamza.

x: God Almighty says, And they disbelieved in it. He says: And they disbelieved in what they asked their Lord for when the punishment descended upon them, and when they witnessed it, in terms of relieving them of it, and that is belief in God, and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought them from God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they disbelieved in it before: meaning in faith in this world. And his statement, And they cast aspersions upon the unseen from a distant place, means: Today they cast aspersions upon Muhammad from a distant place, meaning that they cast aspersions upon him and upon what he brought them of the Book of God based on conjectures and illusions.

x: Some of them say: He is a magician, some of them a poet, and so on. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And they cast the unseen from a distant place, he said: Their statement is that of a magician, rather he is a soothsayer, rather he is a poet.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they cast doubt on the unseen from a distant place. That is, they cast doubt on conjecture, saying: There is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hell.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They are casting about the unseen from a distant place, he said: about the Qur’an.

x: God Almighty says: And a barrier was placed between these polytheists when they were terrified, so there was no escape, and they were seized from a nearby place, so they said, We believe in it. “And between what they desired,” at that time of belief in what they had disbelieved in in the world before that, and they had no way to it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ismail bin Hafs Al-Abli told me: Al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
, he said: They will be prevented from believing in God.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Samad, he said:
m: I heard al-Hasan, and he was asked about this verse,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
, he said: They will be prevented from faith.

c: Ibn Abi Ziyad told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And they will be prevented from what they desire. He said: They will be prevented from faith.

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Samad Al-Ansari told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
. He said: From returning to the world so that they may repent.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
. The people desired to obey God, and they would have done so in this world when they saw what they saw.

c: Al-Hasan bin Wadh told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Habib told us, he said: Abu Al-Ashhab told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
, he said: They will be prevented from faith.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They will be prevented from what they desire of money, children, and worldly pleasures.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire
, he said: of wealth, children, or prosperity.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire

, he said: In the world that they were in and in life. We chose the statement we chose in this regard because the people only wished, when they witnessed the punishment of God, what God had told us about them wishing for, and they said, We believe in it. So God said, And how can they attain that from a distant place, when they had disbelieved before that in this world? If that is the case, then His statement,
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire

, is more appropriate for it to be a statement that they have no way except what they wished for than to be a statement about anything else. And His statement, as He did with their followers before, means that we did with these polytheists, so we stood between them and what they desired of belief in God when God’s wrath descended upon them and they witnessed His punishment, just as we did with their followers because of their disbelief in God from the disbelieving nations before them. We did not accept their belief at that time, just as we did not accept it at a similar time from their peers. Ash’a is the plural of shi’a, and shi’a is the plural of shi’a, so ash’a is the plural of plural. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, As He did with their followers before, he said: the infidels before them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: as He did with their followers before, meaning in this world, if they saw the punishment, their faith would not be accepted from them. And His statement, Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt, means the Most High says: And between these polytheists, when they witnessed the punishment of God, and belief, a barrier was placed between them. Indeed, they were before in this world in doubt about the punishment that had descended upon them and which they witnessed.

c: And their prophet had informed them that
m: if they did not repent from what they were Surat Saba 34:54
h
And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire

, just as was done with their followers before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt. doing, disbelief in God and worshipping idols, God would destroy them and bring upon them His punishment in this world and the Hereafter before it descended upon them. Disquieting means: causing its owner who is in it what makes him doubtful of harm, from their saying: A man has become doubtful: if he has committed a doubt and committed an immoral act, as the rajaz poet said: Oh people, what do I have to do with Abu Dhu’ayb? When you came to him from his absence He smells my affection and flaunts my clothes as if I had made him suspicious He says: It is as if I came to him with suspicion.

notes.en: This is the second hemistich of a verse that became a proverb. It is also transmitted with “Jufaynah” instead of “Juhaynah,” and some say “Ḥufaynah.” Its first hemistich is “Every caravan asks about her father,” with other variants as well. The verse is attributed to Ghuṣayn ibn Ḥayy and also to al-Akhnas ibn Kaʿb. See Kitāb al-Amthāl by Abū ʿUbayd, p. 201; al-Fākhir by al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Salamah, p. 126; and Majmaʿ al-Amthāl by al-Maydānī, 2:319. More likely, this proverb was spoken by one of the transmitters. Al-Qurṭubī cited the report in his Tafsīr, 14:314–315, and al-Tadhkirah, 2:525–526. Ibn Kathīr, in his Tafsīr, 6:515, alluded to the compiler’s inclusion of this report, saying: “Then he—meaning al-Ṭabarī—cited in this connection a wholly fabricated report.”

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 556. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 5:241–242, to Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 556، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 241، 242 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Omitted in: M, T1, T2. The adopted wording is from the original, as in Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ت 2. والمثبت من الأصل كما في تفسير القرطبي.

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī cited it in al-Tibyān, 8:373; al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr, 6:407; al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr, 14:317; Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, 7:294; and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 6:516. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 5:242, to the compiler and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 8/ 373، والبغوى في تفسيره 6/ 407، والقرطبي في تفسيره 14/ 317، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 7/ 294، وابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 516، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 242 إلى المصنف وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān cited it in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, 7:294, with the wording: “assailing the Qurʾān by saying, ‘Tales of the ancients.’”
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 7/ 294 بلفظ: "طاعنين في القرآن بقولهم: أساطير الأولين".

notes.en: In M, T1, T2: “and not.”
notes.ar: في م، ت 1، ت 2: "ولا".

notes.en: The original, T1, T2 read “al-Aylī.” The reading adopted from M is correct. See al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl, 2:165, and Tahdhīb al-Kamāl, 3:62. Ibn Ḥajar explicitly gives his lineage letter by letter in Taqrīb al-Tahdhīb, 1:68.
notes.ar: في الأصل، ت 1، ت 2: "الأيلى". والمثبت من م هو الصواب، وينظر الجرح والتعديل 2/ 165، وتهذيب الكمال 3/ 62، ونصَّ على نسبته بالحروف الحافظ ابن حجر في تقريب التهذيب 1/ 68.

notes.en: Not present in: M, T1, T2.
notes.ar: ليس في: م، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: Al-Fasawī reported it in al-Maʿrifah wa-l-Tārīkh, 2:40, through the chain of Abū al-Ashhab. Ibn Kathīr cited it in his Tafsīr, 6:516. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 5:242, to Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: أخرجه الفسوي في المعرفة والتاريخ 2/ 40 من طريق أبي الأشهب به، وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 516، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 242 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported it in his Tafsīr, 2:133, from al-Thawrī, from someone who had related it to him, from al-Ḥasan.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 133 عن الثورى عمن حدثه عن الحسن.

notes.en: See Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī, 14:318.
notes.ar: ينظر تفسير القرطبي 14/ 318.

notes.en: In M: “He said: He related to me.”
notes.ar: في م: "قال: ثني".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 556; also transmitted through him by al-Firyābī, as cited in Taghlīq al-Taʿlīq, 4:289, but without the words “or a flower.” Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 5:242, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 556 ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 289 - دون قوله: "أو زهرة"، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 242 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: In M it is followed by “in.”
notes.ar: بعده في م: "في".

notes.en: In the original, T2: “al-tanāwush.”
notes.ar: في الأصل، ت 2: "التناوش".

notes.en: In the original, M: “and then.”
notes.ar: في الأصل، م: "فإذا".

notes.en: Omitted in: M, T1, T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: In the original: “and we gathered.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "وحلنا".

notes.en: In M it is followed by “just as.”
notes.ar: بعده في م: "كما".

notes.en: In M, T1: “we accept.”
notes.ar: في م، ت 1: "نقبل".

notes.en: Omitted in: M.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Omitted in: T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 2.

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 556, in an extended form; also transmitted through him by al-Firyābī, as cited in Taghlīq al-Taʿlīq, 4:289. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr, 5:242, to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 556 مطولًا، ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 289 - وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 242 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Omitted in: M, T1, T2.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ت 2.

notes.en: The verse appears unattributed in Iṣlāḥ al-Manṭiq, 1:142; in Lisān al-ʿArab, roots ʾ-t-y, r-y-b, and b-z-z, it is attributed to Khālid ibn Zuhayr.
notes.ar: البيت في إصلاح المنطق 1/ 142 غير منسوب، وفى اللسان (أ ت ى)، (ر ي ب)، (ب ز ز) منسوبًا لخالد بن زهير.

notes.en: “Ātawtuhu” is a dialectal form of “ataytuhu.” See Lisān al-ʿArab, root ʾ-t-y.
notes.ar: "أَتَوْتُه" لغةٌ في "أَتَيْتُه". كما في اللسان (أ ت ى).

notes.en: In M, T1, T2, and the two sources cited for the report: “he smells.” The two forms have the same meaning.
notes.ar: في م، ت 1، ت 2، ومصدرى التخريج: "يشم". وهما بمعنًى.

notes.en: The ʿaṭf of anything is its side; a person’s ʿaṭf extends from his head to his hip. “He pulls my garment toward himself” is the meaning of yabuzzu thawbī. See Lisān al-ʿArab, roots ʿ-ṭ-f and b-z-z.
notes.ar: عطف كل شيء: جانبه. وعطف الإنسان: من لدُن رأسه إلى ورِكه. ويبز ثوبي: أي يَجذِبه إليه. ينظر اللسان (ع ط ف)، (ب ز ز).

notes.en: In the original it is followed by: “The part has been completed from among the parts of…” then an unclear word, and then “may God have mercy on him.”
notes.ar: بعده في الأصل: "تم الجزء من أجزاء" ثم كلمة غير واضحة، ثم "رحمه الله".
